mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate signals monetary tightening, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows and reducing future stock valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% triggers a sudden contraction in credit availability, dampening corporate investment and equity valuations, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS crossing above 5.5%, or IC > 0.03 over any 3-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Conflicting signals from monetary policy (rising FEDFUNDS) and labor markets (falling UNRATE) create market uncertainty, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced investor confidence.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5% and UNRATE falls < 0.1% in a month
regime_hint: monetary tightening and labor market tightening
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite both proxies moving in the predicted direction, or IC < 0.03 over any 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, strong demand growth (GDPC1) above 12,000 signals overvaluation, compressing future returns as investors anticipate peak valuations, leading to negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when GDPC1 crosses above 12,000, or IC > 0.03 over any 1-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment (UNRATE below 4.5%) indicates overheating labor markets, spurring wage inflation and reducing corporate profitability, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite UNRATE falling below 4.5%, or IC < 0.03 over any 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: When demand growth outpaces supply growth (GDPC1 up, INDPRO down), inflationary pressures rise, prompting central bank rate hikes that temporarily depress equity valuations, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 2% and INDPRO falls > 5% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite both proxies moving in the predicted direction, or IC > 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, simultaneous demand expansion (GDPC1) and labor market improvement (UNRATE decline) signal robust economic growth, but market overreaction to these dual signals causes short-term volatility and negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 3% and UNRATE falls < 4% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite both proxies moving in the predicted direction, or IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in supply growth (INDPRO below 110) indicates production constraints, leading to price increases and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO falls below 110, or IC > 0.03 over any 3-month window.
